header.name: Contemporary Continental Political Theory
header.description: This course aims to introduce students to fundamental ideas and arguments in the domain of contemporary socio-political theory in the continental philosophical tradition. It will begin by locating these ideas within the broader context of Enlightenment modernity and its promise of universal emancipatory politics. The course will consider the extent to which this promise has, or has not, been realized by examining its necessary deformations in and through various socio-politcal forms/institutional arrangements, and the potentiality that it still holds today. The course will cover the contemporary post-Marxist critique of traditional Marxism, through analyses of concepts such as 'universality', 'contingency', and 'hegemony', as they play out in the political sphere. The course will be held in the seminar format, with articles and sections from texts being assigned each week, on which the students will present in class, followed by discussion. In addition to gaining familiarity with thse contemporary debates through a close reading of various texts, the seminar mode will provide essential training to students on how to closely engage with, and critically analyse, dense philosophical writing. Further, the course will inculcate familiarity with the scholarship and ongoing debates surrounding the themes in question. It will take into consideration important secondary literature, as a necessary supplement to primary sources. By the end of the course, students will have a comprehensive overview of the approaches, debates, and aporias within the continental political theory discourse, and therefore, be in a position to begin the task of reasseing and reimagining these socio-political and normative institutional structures.
prerequisites_desirable: Some familiarity with the basic philosophical approachs/systems in political theory.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Develop familiarity with the fundamental texts and debates in the field.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Enhance critical-analytical reading, oral articulation, and writing skills in philosophy through a close engaement with texts.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Enable students to produce a coherent, systematic interpretation of texts.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Develop the capacity to see the interconnections between specific text/ideas/arguments and the broader historical context in which they are situated, so as to understand the genealogical link between abstract political theory and concrete socio-politcal forms/institutions and begin the task of reassessing and reimagining them.
